summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency and throughput requirements. Aurora Cloud runs customer-facing generation and streaming chat use-cases; they are evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for a mix of low-latency real-time chat (p95 150-200ms for short prompts) and high-throughput batch generation. Key concerns: concurrency, streaming support, token/sec benchmarks, KV/prefix caching, SSO/KMS for security. Agreed next steps: share detailed benchmarks, run 2-week pilot with dedicated pool or hosted reserved capacity, schedule infra deep dive.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs
transcript: [00:00] Alex Chen (Redwood AE): hi everyone, thanks for joining, im Alex, i run the eenterprise motion for Redwood, with me is Samir our SE.
extra_transcript_1: [00:08] Lisa Gomez (Aurora): hey, thanks, quick intros — im lisa, cto, we own the product infra for our conversational assistant, mark is our ml lead and jenna does infra and network.
extra_transcript_2: [00:20] Mark Rivera (Aurora): morning, yes, our main ask is: we need low p95 latency for interactive chat and also high token throughput for nightly generation jobs, so we're trying to understand if Redwood hosted is ok or if we need dedicated or private deploy.
extra_transcript_3: [00:35] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): got it. could you share target p95 and concurrency numbers? like what do you consider acceptable for the interactive path and whats typical concurrent users?
extra_transcript_4: [00:45] Mark: for chat we want p95 in the 150-250ms range for short prompts (~40-80 tokens), and for longer streams maybe p95 under 500ms per partial chunk. Concurrency: peak about 600 concurrent requests, sustained 200-300. For batch we do spikes up to 5k tokens/sec across the fleet, nightly jobs run in parallel - tokens/sec is important because it affects cost.
extra_transcript_5: [01:15] Jenna: network wise we have a VPC and strict egress rules, so private or VPC peering matters. Also we need KMS for encryption of keys and SOC2 attestation for audits.
extra_transcript_6: [01:28] Alex: totally — those are common. quick framing: hosted is fastest to start and supports streaming and our model catalog, but if you need guaranteed throughput/latency at scale we recommend Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and for regulatory or strict network controls Private (VPC/on-prem). We can do performance fallbacks too - like route by latency or cost.
extra_transcript_7: [01:47] Samir: on the p95 numbers: short context and model choice matter a lot. eg an 8k-context open model we often see p95s of 100-200ms on A100/RTX-class hardware for short decode lengths with optimized kernels, but that changes with concurrency and batching. Caching helps a ton — prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts reduces wall time and tokens processed.
extra_transcript_8: [02:15] Mark: when you say caching, is that at the prefix level on Redwood runtime or do we need to manage embed caches ourselves?
extra_transcript_9: [02:25] Samir: Redwood runtime supports KV/prefix caching automatically for conversational use-cases; you can configure retention and cache keys. That reduces tokens/sec load and lowers cost, but you need to consider cache warm-up for cold starts. Also continuous batching will increase throughput but can increase tail latency, so theres a tradeoff.
extra_transcript_10: [02:50] Lisa: whats your typical tokens/sec numbers for sustained workloads? we benchmarked some other vendors and saw huge variation.
extra_transcript_11: [02:58] Samir: tokens/sec is hardware + model + quantization dependent. As a rough ballpark on a 4xA100 pool with optimized kernel + INT8 quant we often get 1.5k-3k tokens/sec per GPU for autoregressive decoding at medium sequence lengths; with batching you can get higher aggregate throughput, e.g. for n parallel requests we hit 10k-25k tokens/sec across a small cluster. but that is very workload specific — we benchmark with your prompts to provide realistic targets.
extra_transcript_12: [03:35] Mark: ok, for benchmarks we run both streaming interactive sessions (low tokens per call) and batch generation (longer sequences). For streaming, we need per-chunk p95 under 400ms consistently because UI shows partial chunks. For batch the cost per token is more important.
extra_transcript_13: [03:55] Alex: makes sense. For hosted we can provide a benchmark harness quickly; for Dedicated we can provision a reserved pool with autoscale policies and do an apples-to-apples latency test. Private will need network setup but we can still run token/sec and p95 profiling once its in place.
extra_transcript_14: [04:10] Jenna: our compliance team will want SOC2 and also audit logs for inference. do you expose per-token traces or just aggregates?
extra_transcript_15: [04:20] Samir: we provide token-level breakdowns in the Console for usage/cost, and tracing hooks plus request-level logs that can be exported to your SIEM. For Private we can forward logs to your stack. KMS integration is supported for key wrapping. sometimes the transcript i get from our internal tooling spells it oddly - but yes we have that capability.
extra_transcript_16: [04:43] Lisa: and fallbacks? if you have a spike and dedicated pool saturates, what happens?
extra_transcript_17: [04:50] Alex: we have routing policies --- can failover to hosted variants or cheaper model variants. For strict SLA customers we recommend burst capacity or hybrid routing to avoid hard failures. We'll work on SLOs and runbooks as part of the pilot.
extra_transcript_18: [05:05] Mark: curious about streaming overhead, is there a different p95 profile for streaming vs single-response? we saw in-house that streaming introduced 30-50ms overhead per chunk.
extra_transcript_19: [05:15] Samir: yes, streaming has more network calls and smaller decodes so there's per-chunk overhead, but our runtime optimizes partial token flush and reduces per-chunk latency. Also chunk size and tokenization strategy matters. We'll include chunking guidance in the pilot plan.
extra_transcript_20: [05:35] Speaker 1 (Customer, low audio): can you also support nllb models?
extra_transcript_21: [05:40] Samir: we support a wide model catalog, and if a model needs custom compilation we can onboard it; there may be additional perf tuning.
extra_transcript_22: [06:00] Alex: ok lets talk numbers for the pilot: propose a 2-week pilot where we run your traffic in a staging-like env. goal: verify p95 <=200ms for 40-80 token chat under 200-300 sustained concurrency and measure tokens/sec for batch jobs. We can run on hosted first or a small dedicated pool depending on your risk appetite.
extra_transcript_23: [06:20] Mark: what instrumentation do you need from our side? we can share sample payloads and histograms of current latency, plus SLOs. we can also provide a service account for the pilot.
extra_transcript_24: [06:30] Samir: send sample payloads, expected cardinality, and a list of top prompt templates. Jenna if you can share network egress requirements or whether VPC peering required. We'll give a benchmark script and a runsheet.
extra_transcript_25: [06:45] Jenna: we will supply payloads and current qps. one question: in Dedicated, how is autoscale and warm-up handled? we dont want cold starts causing high p95s.
extra_transcript_26: [06:55] Samir: autoscale policies can be smoothing with a standby buffer and warm pool; also we can pre-warm KV cache for known prefixes. For dedicated we configure reserve capacity and burst options to avoid cold starts. For extremely latency-sensitive endpoints we recommend pinned instances or a small always-on pool.
extra_transcript_27: [07:15] Lisa: pricing angle: how do tokens/sec and batching affect cost?
extra_transcript_28: [07:22] Alex: cost is influenced by GPU hours and tokens processed. batching and caching reduce effective tokens processed and improve GPU utilization lowering unit cost. Redwood Optimize can provide recommendations on quantization and batching to hit p95 and cost targets. We'll show you cost simulations in the deck.
extra_transcript_29: [07:38] Mark: any quirks with quantization and accuracy? we care about generation quality for customer-facing models.
extra_transcript_30: [07:44] Samir: quantization can change perplexity and some generation artifacts; our R&D team provides recommended quantization profiles per model and runs evals with your prompts to ensure quality stays within an agreed threshold.
extra_transcript_31: [08:05] Alex: ok recapping next steps: Alex to send perf deck + pricing; Samir to send pilot plan and benchmark harness; Jenna to share payloads and qps; schedule infra deep dive. Any other concerns?
extra_transcript_32: [08:18] Lisa: please include SOC2 report and details on audit logs, and a short note about KMS integration for Private deployments.
extra_transcript_33: [08:28] Samir: will attach SOC2 and a short KMS integration doc. we'll also propose a test that exercises KV cache and streaming so we can measure per-chunk p95 and end-to-end latency.
extra_transcript_34: [08:40] Mark: timeline wise we want to decide by EoQ (end of quarter), so having the results the week after the pilot would be ideal.
extra_transcript_35: [08:48] Alex: understood — we'll target delivering results and a recommendations memo within 7 days after pilot end. thanks all!
notes: Transcript includes occasional mis-attributions and filler words; timestamps approximate. References: performance deck link (https://redwood.ai/perf-deck) and benchmark sheet placeholder (link to be sent).
